svg.title: How surface-mount parts arrive: tape, reel, tube and tray
svg.desc: Four panels, not to the same scale. Top: 8 mm carrier tape, enlarged, drawn to scale: sprocket holes 1.5 mm across every 4 mm along one edge only, pockets every 4 mm holding chip parts lying across the tape, with their ends towards and away from the sprocket holes, a clear cover tape sealed over the pockets, and empty pockets at the leading end as leader, with an arrow showing the direction of feed. Middle left: a 178 mm (7 in) reel with tape coming off the top to the right, so the reel turns clockwise. Middle right: a plastic tube about 500 mm long holding a row of SOIC chips, with a stopper in each end. Bottom: a tray about 323 by 136 mm with a grid of pockets, each holding a large chip.

g.text: Thousands of parts on one tape
Feeds one pocket at a time
50–100 parts in a row, fed by vibration
For large or delicate chips (QFPs, BGAs)
Pin 1 the same way in every pocket
Sprocket holes on one side only
So tape up to 24 mm wide loads only one way
Empty pockets at the leading end: leader
Panels not to the same scale; the tape is enlarged and drawn to scale.
Tape and reel sizes per EIA-481.
